_comment: Course mappings approved by the Senate for the Old UGARC to New UGARC transition,
transcribed from data/policy/course_mapping_ugarc.pdf (DOAA, Course_mapping_data.pdf).
Only the mappings that structural inference cannot derive, or would derive wrongly,
are listed here. A plain suffix drop such as AE641A -> AE641 is already handled by
the stem rule in aptg_ingest.codes and is not repeated.
Three kinds appear:
renumbered  - the course number itself changed, so the codes share no stem and no
structural rule can connect them. PHY102A became PHY112.
corrected   - the stem rule would produce an answer, and it would be the wrong
one. MSE497A maps to MSE498, not to MSE497 -- and MSE497 exists
separately as the new code for MSE398A. Inferring here would
silently credit a student for a course they did not take.
department  - a whole department renumbered. IMExyzA is equivalent to DMSxyz,
stated in general terms in the Senate letter and applied as a rule
rather than enumerated.
One-to-many mappings, where a legacy course maps to a choice or a combination of
new ones, are not aliases and live in course_equivalences.json instead.
These matter for students admitted in Y21 and earlier, whose transcripts carry the
old codes. Without them a Y21 student entering PHY102A is told the course is
unknown, and the requirement it satisfies is scheduled again.
citation: Senate meeting 2023-24/5th (564th), 06-07 June 2024, and SUGC 2024-25/4th-8th; DOAA Course_mapping_data.pdf

aliases.note: UGP-3. The stem rule would give MSE497, which is the new code for MSE398A.

department_rules.text: In general, IMExyzA is equivalent to DMSxyz, while MBAxyz remains unchanged.
department_rules.note: Applied only where the resulting DMS code exists in the course table, and only after the explicit aliases above, which override it.
